NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE LOCAL COUNCILS
NORTH‑WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE LOCAL COUNCILS (RECOVERY OF
TAXES) RULES, 1980
[Gazette of N.‑W. F. P.,
Extraordinary, 10th June, 1.980]
No. S. O. (LG‑II) LG‑1‑14/80.‑In
exercise of the powers conferred by section 172, read with section 139 of the
North‑West Frontier Province, Local Government Ordinance, 1979, the
Government of North‑West Frontier Province, is pleased to make the
following rules, namely:‑
1. Short title and commencement.‑‑(1) These rules
may be called the North‑West Frontier Province, Local Councils (Recovery
of Taxes) Rules, 1980.
(2) They shall come into force
at once.
2. Definitions.‑In these
rules, unless the context otherwise requires‑
(a) "Chairman" means
the Chairman of the Local Council;
(b) "Costs of recovery" includes the charges specified in
these rules;
(c) "defaulter" means
any person from whom any amount is recoverable under these rules and which has
remained unpaid after the presentation of a ‑bill to him under rule 3;
(d) "form" means a
form appended to these rules;
(e) "Ordinance" means the North‑West Frontier
Province Local Government Ordinance, 1979; and
(f) "Taxation
Officer" means the Officer Incharge of the Taxation Department of the
Local Council and any other Officer declared by the Local Council to be Taxation
Officer for the purposes of these rules.
3. Presentation of Bills for taxes. (1) When any amount
on account of a tax shall have become due, the Taxation Officer shall, with the
least practicable delay, cause to be presented to the person liable for the
payment thereof a bill for the sum claimed as due.
(2) Every such bill shall
specify‑----
(a) the period for which, and
the property, occupation or thing in respect of which the sum is claimed;
(b) the liability to be
incurred in the event of default; and
(c) the time within which and
the authority to whom an appeal may be preferred against such claim.
4. Notice of demand.‑(1) If the sum for which any bill has been
presented under rule 3 is not paid within fifteen days from the presentation
thereof, the Taxation Officer may cause to be served upon the defaulter a
notice of demand in Form‑I.
(2) For every notice of demand,
a charge of one rupee shall be levied to cover the cost of the notice and its
service, and such charge shall be included in the tax to be recovered from the
defaulter.
5. Issue of warrants.‑(1) If the defaulter does not within
fifteen days of the service of the notice of demand‑
(a) pay the sum demanded in the
notice of demand; or
(b) show cause to the
satisfaction of the Chairman why he should not pay the same;
The Chairman may direct that
the tax with all costs of recovery shall be recovered under a warrant by
distress and sale of the movable property belonging to the defaulter, or by
attachment and sale of the immovable property belonging to him.
(2) The warrant issued under
sub‑rule (1) shall be in Form‑II, and shall be signed by the
Chairman.
(3) Where the property is
situate within the limits of the Local Council the warrant shall be addressed
to the Taxation Officer, and where the property is outside the Local area of
the Local Council, to the Collector of the district concerned:
Provided that the Officer to
whom the warrant is addressed may endorse such warrant to a subordinate
Officer.
(4) For every warrant issued
under this rule, a sum of five rupees shall be charged, and this amount shall
be included in the cost of recovery.
6. Powers of Entry.‑Any Officer charged with the execution of
a warrant under rule 5 may if authorised by the Chairman by a general or
special order in writing between sunrise and sunset, break, open any outer or
inner door or window of a building in order to make the distress‑‑
(a) if he has reasonable
grounds for believing that such building contains property which is liable to
such distress;
(b) if after notifying his authority and purpose and duly demanding
admittance, he cannot otherwise obtain admittance;
